provenance.author: separate AI author; synthetic; not independent human or external evaluation
provenance.authoring_method: A separately delegated AI authored natural-language task rules, structured rule contracts, full observation snapshots, and expected decisions before inspecting any existing task implementation or scorer. Expected decisions were manually specified, then checked by a separate local three-valued arithmetic/logic script. After drafting, timeline scheduling was adapted to the experiment host acquisition contract: six even-session acquisition opportunities separated by one stable intervening session. This apparatus constraint was supplied by the implementation agent; task rules and manual expected decisions remained author-controlled.
provenance.authored_against: The parent-provided goal of six cases across three distinct evidence-dependency families and the repository AGENTS.md; no existing cases.py, task_context.py, scoring.py, task resolver, EAL implementation, or model outputs were inspected.
authoring_limits: This is a small synthetic convenience corpus, not a sampled population of engineering tasks.
The separate author is another AI agent in the same orchestration session; this is not independent human authorship, blinded external evaluation, or an independently replicated study.

Rules use only declared scalar comparisons, conjunction, disjunction, freshness, explicit invalidation, and exact scope/version applicability. They do not establish general language understanding or performance on open-ended engineering judgement.
Each timeline is a complete synthetic evidence snapshot. Snapshot updates describe possible task changes; they do not model how a deployed system detects unannounced changes.
Expected outcomes and event annotations are evaluation-only data and must be withheld from both model arms and from production decision logic.
The local checker validates fixture consistency with the declared rules. It does not validate a host implementation, EAL runtime, evidence acquisition mechanism, or model behaviour.
No model calls, external data collection, human adjudication, or empirical effectiveness measurement were used to author this corpus.

Stable one-minute intervals were deliberately constructed to permit a fixed 60-second snapshot validity period. This schedule does not measure detection of unannounced within-period changes, and any claims about reuse must retain that assumption.

evaluation_contract.timeline_semantics: Sessions are numbered 0 through 10. now_minute is absolute within a case. facts is the complete available snapshot, not a delta. Do not carry omitted observations into a later snapshot.
evaluation_contract.eligibility: For a requirement, eligible observations have matching fact_key, status active, exact equality on every requirement.scope_keys entry between observation.scope and timeline.scope, and age = now_minute - observed_at_minute satisfying 0 <= age <= max_age_minutes. Extra scope keys do not constrain a requirement.
evaluation_contract.selection: Select the eligible observation with greatest observed_at_minute. Fixtures have no tied newest observations for a fact_key. If none is eligible, the requirement is unknown. Newer eligible observations supersede older eligible values; a historical refutation cannot overrule a newer success.
evaluation_contract.comparisons: eq means typed scalar equality; booleans and numbers are distinct. lte and gte compare numeric values inclusively with expected_value.
evaluation_contract.conjunction: A conjunction is true if every requirement is true, false if any requirement is false, and unknown otherwise.
evaluation_contract.disjunction: For any_of, evaluate each alternative as the conjunction of its requirement_ids. The disjunction is true if any alternative is true, false if every alternative is false, and unknown otherwise.

rule_types.any_of: Disjoin the conjunctions declared in rule.alternatives.
rule_types.versioned_all_of: Conjoin every requirement using its own scope_keys, including version bindings. Truth rules are otherwise identical to all_of.

evaluation_contract.acquisition_schedule: A fresh source snapshot is available at sessions 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10. Odd sessions repeat the immediately preceding facts and scope with current time advanced by one minute. Every expected decision is stable across that one-minute interval. Snapshot reuse for at most 60 seconds is an explicit experimental assumption, not inferred evidence that a source cannot change.
evaluation_contract.identity_binding: specification.identity_scope_keys are stable task identity fields. Every timeline.scope must match specification.scope on those fields before evaluation. Fields absent from identity_scope_keys may legitimately change as declared in the timeline; their requirement-level applicability is governed by requirement.scope_keys.

specification.title: Three independent release obligations
specification.natural_language_rule: The release is ready exactly when integration tests pass, its artifact signature is verified, and its rollback rehearsal passes. Each obligation must have eligible evidence for the same service, environment, and release. Any eligible failed obligation makes the release not_ready even if another obligation is unknown; otherwise missing eligible support makes it undetermined.
specification.scope_description: Readiness of checkout-api release r17 in staging; no production claim.
specification.evidence_policy: Each timeline entry is the complete available observation snapshot for that session. Apply the shared eligibility, newest-observation, and three-valued decision rules. A snapshot can retain historical observations; absence is not evidence of falsehood.

specification.title: Cutover consistency, recovery, and replication
specification.natural_language_rule: The orders cutover is ready exactly when the target schema is compatible, a backup restore is verified, and replica lag is at most 8 seconds. These are independent obligations for the named dataset, environment, and migration. An eligible incompatible-schema result, failed restore, or lag above 8 seconds makes the cutover not_ready. If none is refuted but any obligation lacks eligible evidence, the result is undetermined.

specification.title: Primary or replica read route
specification.natural_language_rule: The read service is ready if either the primary is reachable and has a valid leader lease, or the replica is reachable and its lag is at most 15 seconds. Each route is a conjunction; the service is their disjunction. One fully supported route is sufficient even when the other route is refuted or unknown. The result is not_ready only when every route has at least one eligible refuting observation; otherwise it is undetermined.

specification.title: Direct transport or authenticated tunnel
specification.natural_language_rule: Dispatch is ready if the direct endpoint resolves and its TLS validation passes, or if the tunnel is authenticated and has at least two free slots. Every condition must have eligible evidence in the requested service and region. A fully supported route suffices. Dispatch is not_ready only when both routes are refuted; if no route is supported and at least one route remains unknown, dispatch is undetermined.

specification.title: Firmware, calibration, and authorization versions
specification.natural_language_rule: The robot rollout is ready exactly when safety tests pass for the current firmware version, actuator calibration passes for the current configuration version, and the operator is authorized under the current policy version. Robot and site must match for every observation. A version change affects only requirements that bind that version key; matching fresh evidence for other requirements remains applicable. Any eligible failure makes the result not_ready; otherwise an unsupported current-version obligation makes it undetermined.

specification.title: Schema coverage and migration approval applicability
specification.natural_language_rule: The migration is ready exactly when the backup covers the current schema, a dry run passes for the current schema and migration versions together, and the runbook is approved for the current migration and policy revision together. Database and environment must always match. Version changes invalidate applicability only where the changed key is required; observations never transfer across a required version mismatch. Any eligible failed obligation makes the result not_ready; otherwise missing current-version evidence makes it undetermined.
